## EMERGENCY PHYSICIAN MEDICAL RECORD 



PATIENT	DOB	MRN	DATE OF SERVICE
Jonathan Davis	10/14/1995	948-20491-A	01/08/2024



CHIEF COMPLAINT: 

Crushed left arm in metal press at NSK Plant. 

## HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 

The patient is a 28-year-old left-handed male who was brought by EMS after his left upper extremity became trapped in an industrial metal press at his workplace. According to the team and plant manager, the machine's safety shutoff failed, cycling onto his arm. Tourniquet was applied in the field. Total entrapment time was approximately 20 minutes before extraction. On arrival, patient is in severe distress, pale, diaphoretic, and hypotensive. 

## PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: 

General: Pale, shivering, anxious, severe pain. Cardiovascular: Tachycardic, weak peripheral pulses. Left Upper Extremity: Extreme crushing injury from the distal third of the humerus downwards. Massive soft tissue loss, open mangled skeletal disruption of the elbow, forearm, and hand. Complete transection of the brachial artery and peripheral nerves. Distal limb is completely cold, pale, insensate, and pulseless. Bone fragments are exposed. Active bleeding noted from wound bed when tourniquet is slightly loosened. 

## DIAGNOSTIC IMPRESSION: 

1. Mangled left upper extremity, unsalvageable crush injury with complete vascular and neurologic disruption. 
2. Traumatic shock secondary to acute blood loss and pain. 

## PLAN: 

Immediate orthopedic trauma consultation (Dr. Marcus Vance). Emergency blood transfusion initiated (2 units PRBC). Transfer directly to operating room for emergent life-saving amputation.

## TECHNIQUE 

Three views of the left humerus, elbow, and forearm. Urgent CT angiography of left upper extremity. 

## FINDINGS 

Skeletal structures of the left forearm and hand show extensive, highly comminuted, open segmental fractures. Disorganization of the carpus. Comminuted, displaced supracondylar fracture of the left humerus with severe bone loss and multiple free-floating cortical fragments. CT angiography demonstrates complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at the level of the distal third humerus. Extensive soft tissue lacerations, muscle belly extrusion, and gas bubbles throughout the facial planes. 

## IMPRESSION 

1. Complete mechanical and vascular disruption of the left upper extremity from the level of the distal humerus distally. 2. Extensively comminuted, open skeletal fractures. Unsalvageable limb.
